title: Damodaran valuation — laddered curriculum
built_from: Valuation Agent doctrine (13 stages, D-01..D-49) + his own worked models in damodaran_source_files/
method_notes: Climb the Bloom ladder for valuation as a whole: recall the rules, understand the why, then produce.

Weight practice toward Stages 7-11 (earnings, tax, reinvestment, growth, terminal value): he says 80% of effort goes on discount rates but valuations actually FAIL on cash flows and growth (MBA Session 04).
Produce, not consume: the Apply/Create rungs are where the skill is built. Reading Damodaran is input; valuing a company end-to-end is the skill.
Every number you choose gets a citation and a sensitivity (the doctrine's computed-or-chosen discipline). Log a rep at a lesson's rung when you finish it; two clean reps advance the ladder.

lessons.concept: Route by company type before valuing
lessons.task: From memory, name the four routes (mature non-financial, financial, young/high-growth, declining) and one thing each changes about the model. Check against the routing card.

lessons.concept: Narrative before numbers
lessons.task: Write, from memory, his one-sentence rule for what comes before the spreadsheet. Then read D-01 and correct yourself.

lessons.concept: Currency choice, riskfree rate, non-default-free governments
lessons.task: Recall the rule for each of D-02/03/04. What makes a rate 'riskfree', and what do you do when the government isn't default-free?

lessons.concept: Mature ERP, implied vs historical, country risk, company exposure
lessons.task: Recall each decision. Where does a company's risk exposure come from — where it's incorporated, or where its revenue is?

lessons.concept: Bottom-up beta, business mix, levering, when regressions are OK
lessons.task: Recall how he builds a bottom-up beta and why he distrusts regression betas. When is a regression beta defensible?

lessons.concept: Synthetic rating, country default burden, leases as debt
lessons.task: Recall how he gets a cost of debt without a bond rating, and why leases count as debt.

lessons.concept: Market-value weights, one company-wide number
lessons.task: Recall: book or market weights? One cost of capital per company or per project? Why.

lessons.concept: Normalizing, R&D as capex, one-off charges, negative earnings
lessons.task: Recall each cleanup he does to reported earnings. Why is R&D reclassified as capital, not an expense?

lessons.concept: Effective vs marginal, convergence, NOLs
lessons.task: Recall: which tax rate now, which at the end, and why they converge. What do NOLs do to near-term taxes?

lessons.concept: Net capex, working capital, acquisitions, sales-to-capital
lessons.task: Recall the four reinvestment components. When do you switch to sales-to-capital instead of capex/depreciation?

lessons.concept: Fundamental growth, analyst forecasts, growth fade
lessons.task: Recall the fundamental-growth equation and why analyst forecasts are not inputs.

lessons.concept: Growth cap, ROIC convergence, terminal share
lessons.task: Recall the two caps on terminal value (growth <= riskfree; ROIC -> cost of capital) and why terminal value dominates.

lessons.concept: Cash, cross-holdings, all debt, options, control
lessons.task: Recall how each of cash, cross-holdings, debt, employee options and control affects value per share.

lessons.concept: Simulation over point estimate; value vs price
lessons.task: Recall why he prefers a distribution to a single number, and the difference between value and price.

lessons.concept: Why implied ERP beats historical
lessons.task: Explain in your own words why he uses an implied ERP. What's wrong with a historical average? Say it out loud before checking.

lessons.concept: Why bottom-up beta, not regression
lessons.task: Explain why a bottom-up beta is more reliable than a stock's own regression beta, and the one case where the regression is defensible.

lessons.concept: Paired parameters that self-cancel
lessons.task: Explain the pattern: currency, default spread, and riskfree-vs-terminal-growth each appear on both sides so choosing inconsistently is the only real error. Which one does NOT cancel, and why is it surfaced?

lessons.concept: Effort vs failure: shift from discount rates to cash flows
lessons.task: Explain his claim that ~80% of effort goes on discount rates but valuations fail on cash flows/growth. What should that change about where YOU spend time?

lessons.concept: Sales-to-capital for growth companies
lessons.example: a sector dataset in damodaran_source_files (e.g. cfspr21.xlsx) — find his sales-to-capital column
lessons.task: Explain why revenue-driven reinvestment (sales-to-capital) fits young/high-growth firms better than capex-depreciation. Find a real sector figure in his dataset.

lessons.concept: Growth is earned, not forecast
lessons.task: Explain growth = reinvestment rate x ROIC, and why plugging in an analyst's growth number is circular/unfounded.

lessons.concept: Why terminal discipline matters most
lessons.task: Explain why terminal value is usually most of the value, and how the growth cap and ROIC-convergence keep it honest.

lessons.concept: Two different games
lessons.task: Explain the difference between valuing (cash flows, risk, growth) and pricing (multiples, mood). When is each the right tool?

lessons.concept: Read a whole valuation against its doctrine
lessons.task: Run the agent on a stable company (e.g. KO). For each flagged judgment, open the cited doctrine card and confirm you understand why that value was chosen. Note any you'd choose differently.

lessons.concept: Build a cost of capital end-to-end
lessons.example: cross-check against his industry cost-of-capital data (wacc)
lessons.task: For one company, work out riskfree, ERP, bottom-up beta, cost of debt and market-value-weighted WACC by hand. Check each against his sector figure. Each number: computed or chosen (with a reason).

lessons.concept: Earnings, tax and reinvestment (where valuations fail)
lessons.example: a completed DCF in damodaran_source_files (see INDEX.md), e.g. Paytm2021.xlsx
lessons.task: For your company: normalize base-year earnings, pick a tax path, and build reinvestment (net capex, working capital, or sales-to-capital). Compare your structure to how he did it in a real model.

lessons.concept: Grow it and close it out
lessons.task: Extend your company's cash flows with fundamental growth and a disciplined terminal value (growth <= riskfree, ROIC -> cost of capital). What share of value is terminal? Is that defensible?

lessons.concept: Trace a finished DCF to the doctrine
lessons.example: open a company DCF from damodaran_source_files (e.g. Paytm2021.xlsx)
lessons.task: Open one of his real DCF spreadsheets. Trace every major input (story, growth, reinvestment, terminal) back to the doctrine stage it belongs to. Where did he make a JUDGMENT vs a computation?

lessons.concept: How the route changes the model
lessons.example: two of his models: a mature company vs a young/high-growth one (e.g. Paytm)
lessons.task: Put two of his DCFs side by side. List the concrete ways the young-growth model differs from the mature one (sales-to-capital, negative earnings, longer high-growth). Tie each difference to a routing decision.

lessons.concept: Disputed constants become paths
lessons.example: any of his multi-year DCF models
lessons.task: In a real model, trace the three convergences: effective->marginal tax, high->terminal growth, excess->competitive returns. Why is 'it's a path, not a constant' the resolution each time?

lessons.concept: Which inputs actually move value
lessons.example: lab: re-run value.py flipping one input at a time
lessons.task: Flip inputs one at a time (beta, margin, growth, terminal ROC) and record how much value moves. Confirm his claim that cash-flow/growth inputs dominate discount-rate inputs.

lessons.concept: You beat the model when you can defend the choice
read: agent/README.md (the resolver hierarchy: User beats Heuristic beats Claude)
lessons.task: Pick one judgment the agent flags high-uncertainty (e.g. terminal ROC, country-risk method). Choose your own value and defend it in writing with a sensitivity — why your number, and what it costs if you're wrong.

lessons.concept: Cheap or dear — and can you defend it
lessons.task: For a company you've valued, deliver a value-vs-price verdict. State the 2-3 assumptions the verdict hangs on, and what would have to be true for the market to be right instead of you.

lessons.concept: Your own end-to-end valuation
lessons.example: lab: build it yourself, using value.py only as a check
lessons.task: Pick a company you actually care about. Write its STORY first (D-01), then build the full valuation producing your own inputs at every stage. This is the produce-not-consume milestone.

lessons.concept: A defensible valuation memo
lessons.task: Turn your valuation into a short memo: the story, the key judgments (each cited to a doctrine point with its sensitivity), a simulation/range, and the value-vs-price verdict. Then GRINDE-map the method so it sticks.
